title: Robotic system not responding with AGVs stopped or out of sync
user_facing_summary: Use this troubleshooting flow when a site reports that robotic operation has stopped, AGVs are not moving or are out of sync, small sort activity has stopped, or the RMS view is blank or abnormal. Confirm the observable system state, inspect service and application evidence, recover the affected service or gateway through an authorized procedure, correct residual AGV state, and validate both service responsiveness and resumed operation.
playbook_goal: Determine whether the site-wide stoppage is associated with an abnormal OptiSweep, WCSWebApplication, or related gateway state; support authorized recovery; identify residual AGV synchronization or state issues; and confirm stable robotic operation before release.
observed_entry_symptoms: Nothing is moving across the site or bots are stopped in multiple areas.
The robotic system is reported as not responding.
Small sort operation is not running.
AGVs are reported out of sync or several AGVs stop after a heartbeat issue.
Totes cannot be removed from the hospital workflow.
RMS or HMI is mostly blank or displays an apparent ".NET Control not created." message.
The site reports no obvious failed AGV even though automated movement has stopped.
negative_or_absent_signals: The site initially reported no specific fault or failed AGV.
The available evidence does not confirm that the Ignition memory trend caused the stoppage.
A successful HTTP response and returned AGV records do not by themselves confirm that all AGVs are synchronized or that production has recovered.
The Windows Services screenshot shows OptiSweep running, but does not establish whether it was running before or after a restart.
support_user_language_examples: We can't get totes out of hospital
Several bots stopped after a heartbeat issue
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible OptiSweep service termination or restart event associated with site-wide stoppage
Possible WCSWebApplication application or database-command fault near the service event
Possible residual AGV synchronization, roster, or state inconsistency after service recovery
Possible abnormal RMS rendering or control-state presentation
Possible webservice memory or log-growth condition requiring follow-up
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns extracted from the incident evidence, not confirmed diagnoses or user-facing entry requirements. Event Viewer showed an OptiSweep Service Control Manager Event 7031 termination and clustered WCSWebApplication errors, while case comments reported AGVs going out of sync and later being corrected in RMS. The memory trend review explicitly said there was no indication that memory caused the crash.
affected_systems_or_components: Windows Event Viewer / Service Control Manager
separability_reason: No separate candidate is emitted. The application/database and memory observations are supporting investigations within the same site-wide stoppage flow; the source does not provide a distinct independent symptom entry or independently validated recovery path for them.
confidence_reason: The packet provides clear observable entry symptoms, named diagnostic surfaces, a source-supported service failure signal, a high-level recovery sequence, residual AGV correction, and multiple validation signals. Exact root cause and the significance of some memory and RMS messages remain uncertain.

nodes.goal: Determine whether the report represents a broad robotic-operation stoppage with an abnormal RMS or HMI presentation rather than an isolated AGV issue.

nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or operator confirms whether the affected area has broad loss of movement, whether the small sort or hospital workflow is also affected, and whether RMS/HMI is blank or shows an abnormal control message. In RMS/HMI, a healthy or alternate pattern is normal populated system status with localized impact only; an unhealthy pattern is broad stopped operation with blank or abnormal system presentation; inconclusive means the scope, affected workflow, or displayed message cannot be confirmed.

A healthy signal is a responding gateway with a current response time and no recent slow-response events; an unhealthy signal is an unavailable or nonresponsive gateway or a clearly abnormal resource trend correlated with the stoppage; inconclusive means the snapshot is stale, the trend lacks labels, or the gateway state cannot be verified.

summary: Use this troubleshooting flow when a site reports that robotic operation has stopped, AGVs are not moving or are out of sync, small sort activity has stopped, or the RMS view is blank or abnormal. Confirm the observable system state, inspect service and application evidence, recover the affected service or gateway through an authorized procedure, correct residual AGV state, and validate both service responsiveness and resumed operation.
